description: LGRIP30 is the Landsat-derived Global Rainfed and Irrigated-Area Product at 30 m from the Global Food-and-Water Security-support Analysis Data project, a NASA-funded project run by the USGS Western Geographic Science Center. The project page says GFSAD has released two global products that can be downloaded from NASA's LP DAAC, the 30 m cropland extent and LGRIP30, with an algorithm theoretical basis document and user guide, and shows LGRIP30 as a map of rainfed and irrigated cropland for the nominal year 2015. The current project phase (2023 to 2028) plans 2020 and 2025 editions of the cropland extent, rainfed and irrigated, cropping intensity and crop type products. Coverage is global croplands at 30 m. Access is free through LP DAAC and a web viewer; USGS media on the page are public domain. Caveats: the LP DAAC download terms were not read, the released edition is for about 2015, and the irrigated and rainfed split is a remote sensing classification. Simulation uses: mapping irrigation water demand and the exposure of irrigated agriculture to drought. Related records: global irrigated areas by Meier et al. (data-global-irrigated-areas-meier-2018) and GMIA next (data-gmia-next-global-irrigated-areas-30m).
